item.text: {"text":"Closest matches support attribute-level matching and context-sensitive text fusion, but do not establish the exact combination of NextItNet, causal convolution, and a text encoder trained from scratch. [MARS (CIKM 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) represents users/items through multiple attribute-aware vectors and scores attribute-wise interactions; useful motivation for preserving specific textual evidence instead of compressing everything into one embedding. Its encoder uses pretrained language models, so its results do not validate scratch-trained text encoding. [Sequence-level Semantic Representation Fusion (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) argues that simple text-plus-ID addition can be ineffective and introduces context-sensitive fusion through Fourier-domain multiplication, interpreted as contextual convolution. This is conceptual support, not evidence that its implementation preserves causal NextItNet behavior.\n\n[ConvRec (IJCAI-ECAI 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04723) explores attribute-aware recommendation through hierarchical convolution with linear computational and memory complexity. It supports investigating convolutional attribute processing, but does not establish the requested scratch-trained title/description setup. A compatible research hypothesis is one NextItNet network with randomly initialized token embeddings, a lightweight jointly trained title/description encoder, and causal-history-conditioned pooling over text tokens, trained with next-item prediction. This adaptation remains unverified by the retrieved studies; compare against ID-only and static text-fusion variants under the pinned validation protocol. Use only supplied titles/descriptions: learned token patterns are statistical evidence, while product compatibility and unmet need remain unobserved unless descriptions explicitly support them."}
